claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a random solid solution with high chemical disorder.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant local lattice distortion.
Annealing or Monte Carlo-driven ordering can transform HfTi or TiZr clusters in HfNbTaTiZr into ordered B2-like structures.
B2 ordering requires a temperature high enough for atomic rearrangement but below melting.
A stoichiometry favoring HfTi or TiZr pairing is required for the proposed ordering.
Ordered HfTi or TiZr B2-like clusters have less local lattice distortion than random HfNbTaTiZr.
The ordered B2-like clusters form percolative pathways for phonon transport.
B2 ordering locally reduces the variance in atomic size and electronegativity.
Reduced local size and electronegativity variance decreases the scattering cross-section for high-frequency phonons.
Reduced lattice distortion shifts the high-frequency phonon DOS peak to higher frequencies.
The higher-frequency states produced by ordering have higher phonon group velocities.
Continuous low-distortion regions provide heat-transport channels that overcome the additional scattering normally associated with chemical short-range order.
Percolated B2-like ordering increases the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr relative to its random state.
The ordered state will exhibit reduced atomic displacement amplitudes or Debye-Waller factors in the ordered regions.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has low thermal conductivity because random lattice distortions and chemical disorder strongly scatter phonons.
A conductivity increase occurs only after ordering exceeds a percolation threshold and creates continuous low-distortion pathways.
Isolated ordered domains or incoherent precipitates instead decrease conductivity by acting as strong phonon-scattering centers.
The proposed effect is limited by B2-phase stability against decomposition into brittle intermetallics or oxides.
The thermal-transport percolation threshold in HfNbTaTiZr is unknown.
Thermodynamic predictions of B2 stability in HfNbTaTiZr are limited by database quality.
